title: Breakdown of Monotonic Impurity Entropy Flow in $\mathscr{PT}$-Symmetric Multichannel Kondo Systems
authors: Pradip Kattel, Abay Zhakenov, Natan Andrei
abstract: We study a $\mathscr{PT}$-symmetric non-Hermitian multichannel Kondo model consisting of a pair of spin-$\frac12$ impurities coupled to $n$ conduction-electron channels through complex-conjugate Kondo couplings. The impurity renormalization-group (RG) flow is characterized by the Kondo scale $T_K$ and a dimensionless non-Hermiticity parameter $α$. As $α$ increases, the exact Bethe Ansatz solution exhibits four impurity phases: overscreened Kondo, zero mode, Yu--Shiba--Rusinov (YSR), and local moment. The Kondo, zero-mode, and local-moment phases are $\mathscr{PT}$-unbroken, whereas the YSR phase spontaneously breaks $\mathscr{PT}$ symmetry. Using a generalized thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz, we determine the impurity free energy and Affleck--Ludwig $g$-function throughout the $\mathscr{PT}$-unbroken phases. In the Kondo phase, the defect RG flow connects the ultraviolet and infrared conformal fixed points, with the impurity entropy flowing from $2\ln2$ to $2\ln\left[2\cos\left(\fracπ{n+2}\right)\right]$, in agreement with defect conformal field theory. In the zero-mode phase, zero-energy impurity strings reorganize the spectrum into multiple excitation towers, while in the local-moment phase, the RG flow becomes cyclic, returning to the unscreened local-moment fixed point. We conjecture that RG irreversibility, and hence a generalized Affleck--Ludwig $g$-theorem, survives throughout the Kondo phase. Our exact solution nevertheless shows that a real spectrum and defect entropies consistent with defect CFT do not guarantee RG irreversibility: the impurity entropy is non-monotonic in both the zero-mode and local-moment phases.
summary: This paper analyzes a $\mathscr{PT}$-symmetric Kondo model to study the entropy flow of impurities. Using advanced techniques like TBA and RG analysis, the authors map out four distinct impurity phases based on a non-Hermiticity parameter $\alpha$. The key finding is that while some phases show expected monotonic behavior, others exhibit nonmonotonic entropy flow, challenging simple assumptions about quantum renormalization group irreversibility.
main_problem: The study investigates the breakdown of monotonic impurity entropy flow within $\mathscr{PT}$-symmetric multichannel Kondo systems.
main_result: While the standard Kondo phase shows monotonic entropy flow consistent with defect CFT, the zero-mode and local-moment phases exhibit nonmonotonic behavior, contradicting simple expectations of RG irreversibility.
method: The analysis employs Renormalization Group (RG) flow techniques combined with a generalized Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz (TBA) to calculate impurity free energy and entropy.
model_or_system: The system is a $\mathscr{PT}$-symmetric non-Hermitian multichannel Kondo model involving two spin-$1/2$ impurities coupled to $n$ conduction electron channels via complex-conjugate couplings.
key_observables: Impurity free energy, Affleck–Ludwig $g$-function, and impurity entropy flow ($\text{Simp}$).
important_parameters: The dimensionless non-Hermiticity parameter $\alpha$, which dictates the phase diagram (Kondo, zero-mode, YSR, local moment).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on exact solutions derived from Bethe Ansatz methods and defect CFT concepts.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the phase diagram mapping $\alpha$ to different Kondo regimes; they also show $\text{Simp}$ vs. $T/T_K$, demonstrating monotonic flow in some phases and nonmonotonicity (overshoots/undershoots) in others.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the model Hamiltonian and parameters, then analyzes the RG flow across different regimes defined by $\alpha$. It details calculations using TBA to find thermodynamic quantities, culminating in a comparison between theoretical expectations of monotonicity and the actual nonmonotonic results found for specific phases.
why_interesting: The investigation into non-Hermitian physics ($\mathscr{PT}$ symmetry) applied to strongly correlated impurity models provides insights into how spectral properties (like complex energies or zero modes) can violate standard thermodynamic theorems like RG irreversibility, which is crucial for understanding open quantum systems dynamics.
